title: Affine test from an excessive even moment
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,j$ be integers with $0<r$, $1\le j$, and $j\le r$. Suppose the second moment of $X$ under $\mathrm{law}$ is $1$; every odd moment of order $2l-1$ is zero for $1\le l\le r$; and for every integer $l$ with $1\le l<j$, the even moment of order $2l$ equals $(2r-1)^l\binom{r}{l}/\binom{2r}{2l}$. If the even moment of order $2j$ is strictly greater than $(2r-1)^j\binom{r}{j}/\binom{2r}{2j}$, then there are real numbers $a,b$ such that the $2r$-norm under $\mathrm{law}$ of $x\mapsto a+bX(x)/\sqrt{2r-1}$ is strictly greater than the $2$-norm under $\mathrm{law}$ of $x\mapsto a+bX(x)$.
